# Overview

In this document, we test our hypothesis that (1) the loss of one leg reduces the probability of losing the homologous leg of the same pair; and (2) the loss of one ambulatory leg reduces the probability of losing another ambulatory leg located on the same side of the body, we employed a Monte Carlo approach. In this approach, we randomized the observed data to generate a null distribution in which the events of interest occur purely by chance. We then compared the observed frequencies in our collected data to those expected under this null model. If the observed frequencies do not differ from the null expectations, this suggests that the patterns arise from random processes. Conversely, significant deviations from the null distribution indicate that additional factors may be influencing the occurrence of these events. 

```{r calling Rpackages}

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(vegan)

```


```{r importing the data}
data_raw <- read.table(here("data","raw","data.tsv"), header = T, stringsAsFactors = T, sep='\t')

str(data_raw)

# reorder the levels of the population factor to ensure they are in the correct temporal order
data_raw <- data_raw %>%
  mutate(population = factor(population, levels = c("TG", "MC", "GE", "GP")))

# creating a presence/absence of autotomy column
data_raw$autotomized <- ifelse(data_raw$total >= 1, 1, 0)

# changing the names of the population to the year they've been collected
data_raw <- data_raw %>%
  mutate(population = recode(population,
    "TG" = "2002",
    "MC" = "2009",
    "GE" = "2011",
    "GP" = "2012"
  ))
```

# The hypothesis

First we established the test statistic, which is the event of interest for each hypothesis.

# Hypothesis 1: how many times an entire pair of legs was lost.

```{r}

leg1 <- sum(data_raw$r1 == 1 & data_raw$l1 == 1)
leg2 <- sum(data_raw$r2 == 1 & data_raw$l2 == 1)
leg3 <- sum(data_raw$r3 == 1 & data_raw$l3 == 1)
leg4 <- sum(data_raw$r4 == 1 & data_raw$l4 == 1)

```


# Hypothesis 2: how many time legs were lost in the same side of the body
* in this hypothesis we are taking into account only the ambulatory legs
* because we do not have the temporal sequence in which the legs were lost, we are also not considering cases in which 3 legs were lost because this inevitabelly would count as a assymetrical lost even if it wasn't the case

```{r}

sideR <- sum(rowSums(data_raw[, c("r1", "r3", "r4")] == 1) == 2)
sideL <- sum(rowSums(data_raw[, c("l1", "l3", "l4")] == 1) == 2)
side <- sideR + sideL

```


# Null simulation

```{r}

simulations = 10

sim.leg1 <- numeric(simulations)
sim.leg2 <- numeric(simulations)
sim.leg3 <- numeric(simulations)
sim.leg4 <- numeric(simulations)
sim.side <- numeric(simulations)

```


Because of the results in the GLMMs, we decided to fix the proportion each population and each leg

# Neste modelo nulo, mantemos fixos:
# - o número de perdas por indivíduo (linhas)
# - a frequência de amputação por tipo de perna (colunas)
# Ou seja, usamos fixedmar = "both".

```{r}

null <- permatfull(data_raw, fixedmar = "both", times = simulations)

for (i in seq_len(simulations)) {
  
  df.null <- as.data.frame(nulo1$perm[[i]])
  
  null_leg1 <- sum(df.null$r1 == 1 & df.null$l1 == 1)
  null_leg2 <- sum(df.null$r2 == 1 & df.null$l2 == 1)
  null_leg3 <- sum(df.null$r3 == 1 & df.null$l3 == 1)
  null_leg4 <- sum(df.null$r4 == 1 & df.null$l4 == 1)
  
  sim.leg1[i] <- null_leg1
  sim.leg2[i] <- null_leg2
  sim.leg3[i] <- null_leg3
  sim.leg4[i] <- null_leg4
  
  sideR_null <- sum(rowSums(df.null[, c("r1", "r3", "r4")] == 1) == 2)
  sideL_null <- sum(rowSums(df.null[, c("l1", "l3", "l4")] == 1) == 2)
  sim.side <- sideR_null + sideL_null
}

```


# P-values

To calculate the p-values using this method, we calculate how frequent it is to find the observed results in the simulations.

```{r}

p_leg1 <- (sum(sim.par1_1 <= par1) + 1) / (length(sim.par1_1) + 1)
p_leg2 <- (sum(sim.par2_1 <= par2) + 1) / (length(sim.par2_1) + 1)
p_leg3 <- (sum(sim.par3_1 <= par3) + 1) / (length(sim.par3_1) + 1)
p_leg4 <- (sum(sim.par4_1 <= par4) + 1) / (length(sim.par4_1) + 1)
p_ladoDE_1 <- (sum(sim.ladoDE_1 <= ladoDE) + 1) / (length(sim.ladoDE_1) + 1)

```


# 6. Fazendo gráficos que mostram a frequência das estatísticas do teste e onde se encontra o valor real observado

dados_plot <- bind_rows(
  
  data.frame(sim = sim.par1, perna = "PAR1", modelo = "Modelo 1"),
  data.frame(sim = sim.par1_1, perna = "PAR1", modelo = "Modelo 2"),
  
  data.frame(sim = sim.par2, perna = "PAR2", modelo = "Modelo 1"),
  data.frame(sim = sim.par2_1, perna = "PAR2", modelo = "Modelo 2"),
  
  data.frame(sim = sim.par3, perna = "PAR3", modelo = "Modelo 1"),
  data.frame(sim = sim.par3_1, perna = "PAR3", modelo = "Modelo 2"),
  
  data.frame(sim = sim.par4, perna = "PAR4", modelo = "Modelo 1"),
  data.frame(sim = sim.par4_1, perna = "PAR4", modelo = "Modelo 2")
)

observados <- data.frame(
  perna = c("PAR1","PAR2","PAR3","PAR4"),
  valor = c(par1, par2, par3, par4)
)

ggplot(dados_plot, aes(x = sim, fill = modelo)) +
  
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    position = "identity",
    alpha = 0.5,
    binwidth = 1,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  
  geom_vline(
    data = observados,
    aes(xintercept = valor),
    color = "#d7301f",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(~perna, ncol = 2) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#bdbdbd", "#3182bd")) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Distribuições nulas das perdas por par de pernas",
    x = "Número de eventos",
    y = "Densidade",
    fill = "Modelo nulo"
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
